entries.text: Nasdaq −2.6% on Thursday; Anthropic's draft prospectus shows $16.3bn H1 revenue. IPO expected in November.
Anthropic's public prospectus (revenue up about 14× in H1, $112bn cash) lifted the Nasdaq over 1% before Big Tech earnings.
Week 44: Anthropic files S-1 (ticker ANT, H1 revenue $16.3bn); Alphabet loses about $500bn in a day, Intel −20%+; Nasdaq −2.0% on the week, SMI +2.4%.

Week 45: Nasdaq about −5.5% on Thursday, worst day since March 2020 (Nasdaq 100 −6.4%); data-center opponents win 38 of 39 local ballots; Anthropic's S-1/A shows ~$17bn Q3 revenue and a $567m operating loss; METR says AI roughly doubled the pace of Anthropic's research.
SVP deadline closed: seven candidates, Aeschi undecided. Vote on 9 December.
Week 44: SVP hearings with eight candidates; committee proposal by 13 Nov, group vote 20 Nov; Greens critical of Amaudruz.
Fed hikes to 3.75–4.00%, first hike since 2023.
US 10-year peaks at 5.36%, highest since 2002.
Bond rally: 10-year back below 5% as money leaves AI stocks. Fed decides 28 Oct.
28 Oct: Fed holds at 3.75–4.00% with two dissents for a hike (Cook, Hammack); futures price a December hike at about 85%. ECB holds at 2.5%; Lagarde to leave 7 Feb 2027.
Week 45: US adds 165,000 jobs in October; futures still lean to a December hike; US 10-year −7 bp to 4.86%; Bank of England hikes in a divided vote and warns of ~5% inflation.

title: Fed, rates and the bond market

entries.text: About 550,000 protest; Limoges town hall burned.
10-year yield briefly above 5%, spread to Bunds near 160 bp; Moody's holds the rating.
Week 44: Q3 GDP contracts; third protest weekend draws about 320,000, down from 550,000.
Week 45: nationwide general strike on 5 Nov over wages and public services; Belgium's coalition also breaks over its budget.
US–Israeli air campaign against Iran begins.
Ceasefire ends the heaviest fighting.
Interim truce collapses; Iran resumes attacks on shipping.
Houthi strikes on Saudi airports and oil sites; Brent at its highest since May; Iran says Hormuz management will change permanently.
Saudi defence minister in Tehran for de-escalation talks; Brent falls about 4.7% from its six-month high.
Houthis claim a strike on Ras Tanura; WSJ says the US and Israel plan short strikes on Iran after the midterms; Qatar hands Tehran a peace proposal.
Washington writes to Tehran to restart truce talks and Gulf states push a deal to reopen Hormuz; oil falls, but the US says strikes resume if talks fail.

Gulf officials say US strikes could come from 4 November; Iran sends a delegation to Doha and calls the US outreach a positive step; October ship attacks in and around Hormuz more than double September's.
Week 44: Saudi, Pakistani and Turkish envoys in Tehran; Vance letter restarts truce talks; Iranian delegation in Doha, while Gulf officials say US strikes could come from 4 Nov.
Talks move to a third day in Doha; Khamenei puts forces on alert and Tehran says it is debating its nuclear-weapons ban.
Oil falls about 6% as Washington and Tehran talk up diplomacy, but Trump says one or two targets remain and Gulf states brace for fighting after the midterms.
Trump conceded the war cost Republicans the midterms but said he would do it again; Democrats plan to use their majority to end it, and Brent fell to near $93 before rebounding.
UKMTO: 11 ships attacked around Hormuz in the week to 6 Nov, three sunk, traffic about 65% below pre-war; Qeshm hit again; Araghchi sets seven conditions to reopen the strait.

Week 45: Doha talks and a 6% oil drop on Monday, then US strikes on Qeshm; UKMTO counts 11 ships attacked and three sunk in the week to 6 Nov; Trump says the war cost the midterms but he would do it again.

US sets up Task Force Iron Gate to close Iran's land routes and the Caspian on top of the naval blockade; a Saudi Aramco building in Riyadh is hit by debris from an intercepted projectile (Al Jazeera).

After meeting Qatar's prime minister, Trump called the war 'effectively over' while Rubio sees no breakthrough; France blamed the Revolutionary Guards for a cyberattack on its supermarkets (AP, France 24).
Israel votes; record turnout of about 78%.
Final count: Netanyahu bloc 53, Eisenkot bloc 48, Arab parties 19; nobody reaches 61. Netanyahu stays caretaker with war powers.
MSCI finalises rules for 'non-operating companies'.
Final list due 11 Nov, effective after 30 Nov; JPMorgan estimates ~$2.8bn of forced selling of the stock.
Week 44: Strategy buys no Bitcoin 19–25 Oct, holds 848,517 BTC, buys back $205m of STRC; MSCI decision date not confirmed this week.
Week 45 (unconfirmed, Bitcoin Treasuries): Strategy buys 811 BTC and spends $208m buying back STRC, which returns to $100.
FINMA approves BBIT, the first retail spot Bitcoin fund; SIX listing in November.
Week 44: BBIT listing on SIX still expected in November; no date announced.
Week 45: BBIT still has no SIX listing date.
Witkoff meets Putin in St. Petersburg; no agreement. Starlink back to full speed after throttling.
Kyiv pauses refinery strikes at US request and the Oleshky local ceasefire holds a third day, while Russia kills 14 in Dnipro.
Week 44: Finland and Norway call Putin; Oleshky local ceasefire holds; Kyiv reportedly pauses refinery strikes at US request; 14 killed in Dnipro.
The US will mediate direct Russia-Ukraine talks in Abu Dhabi next week, after a Russian strike killed 29 people at an aid center.
After meeting Putin's envoy Kirill Dmitriev, Trump promised a "big agreement" that could involve more than Ukraine, ahead of talks in Abu Dhabi next week (International Intrigue).
Week 45: US to mediate Russia–Ukraine talks in Abu Dhabi; Russia strikes Kyiv's Northern Bridge and power; EU's Kallas rejects Trump's 'very big' deal covering all of Europe.
US, Russian and Ukrainian officials meet in Abu Dhabi on 10–11 Nov, the first direct talks in nine months; France says Europeans will join.
Democrats won both chambers of Congress, including Senate seats in Texas and Kansas; Trump congratulated them and pledged to work across the aisle.
Week 45: Democrats win both chambers, including Senate seats in Texas and Kansas; Vance blames the Iran war; Republicans press Trump to fire Hegseth; subpoenas for Trump-linked firms in preparation.
